sentences.text: As per prosecution case, FIR was lodged on 07.04.2023 about incident of rape which occurred on 31.03.2023.
As per FIR, petitioner took the prosecutrix to the farmhouse in Mangeli and has committed rape upon her promising to get a job for her.
Prosecutrix is aged about 33 years.
Charge sheet was filed against the petitioner and charges were framed vide order dated 09.11.2023 for offence under Section 376 of the IPC.

3. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submitted that false report was lodged against the petitioner and during pendency of litigation, prosecutrix has compromised the matter with petitioner and she does not want to prosecute him before the Court of law.

Compromise between the parties was also verified by Registrar (Judicial-II) on 25.09.2023, wherein it was stated that victim was not under any threat, inducement or pressure and she has entered into the compromise and settled the matter with petitioner.
On the basis of aforesaid, counsel for petitioner has made a prayer for quashing of charge sheet and consequential criminal proceedings arising out of it.
4. Learned Government Advocate appearing for the State opposed the prayer and submitted that offence is non-compoundable in nature and having serious consequences over society.
In these circumstances, permission may not be granted for compounding.

5. Heard the counsel for the parties.
6. Compounding of the cases is one thing and quashing of case exercising power under Section 482 of Code of Criminal Procedure is another thing.
7.

In case of B.S. Joshi Vs. Haryana reported in (2003) 4 SCC 675, the non-compoundable offence under Section 498-A of the IPC was quashed exercising inherent power under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure in view of compromise between the parties.

entities.text: B.S. Joshi Vs. Haryana reported in (2003) 4 SCC 675
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In case of Nikhil Marchant Vs. CBI reported in (2008) 9 SCC 677, Court again exercised its inherent power facing reliance on B.S. Joshi (supra) and quashed the case for non- compoundable offences under Sections 420, 467,
468 and 471 of the IPC read with Section 13(2) and 13(1) (D) of Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.

entities.text: Nikhil Marchant Vs. CBI reported in (2008) 9 SCC 677
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Apex Court in case of Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab reported in (2010) 15 SCC 118 has held that heinous and serious offences of mental depravity or offences like murder, rape, dacoity etc. can not be fittingly quashed even though the victim or victim's family and offender have settled their dispute.

entities.text: Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab reported in (2010) 15 SCC 118
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Such offences are not private in nature and have serious impact on society.

Similarly,
offences under special statutes like Prevention of Corruption Act or offence committed by public servant while working in official capacity cannot be quashed.
Criminal cases having overwhelmingly pre-dominantingly civil flavour can be quashed as said offences are private and personal in nature and quashing will not affect society at large.

It is further held in said judgment that the High Court may quash criminal proceedings, if in its view because of the compromise between offender and victim, the possibility of conviction is remote and bleak and continuation of criminal case would put accused to great oppression and prejudice and extreme injustice would be caused to him by not quashing criminal case despite full and complete settlement and compromise with the victim.
8.
In this case, petitioner has filed an application for retrieving whatsapp chat between Mobile No.9343516435, 7470458808 and Mobile No.9424876968.

Said prayer was made as prosecutrix has Brijesh Singh Thakur vs State Of M.P. on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151469243/
2 admitted that petitioner has falsely been implicated for demand of money.

sentences.text: Prayer was rejected and charges were framed against the petitioner.
9. On going through the facts of the case, it is found that petitioner is said to have taken the prosecutrix in a farmhouse and has committed rape with her to secure a job for her.
Incident is said to have occurred on 31.03.2023 but she did not lodge any report immediately at Police Station.
Report was lodged on 07.04.2023 after delay of about one week.
Prosecutrix is major aged about 33 years and petitioner is aged about 49 years.
Prosecutrix was examined on 07.04.2023 and no signs and symptoms of forced intercourse were found.
Prosecutrix is a married woman having two children.
She is living along with her mother and children.
She agreed to enter into physical relationship with petitioner on promise for securing her a job.
Promise to give material benefits is different from promise to marry a woman.
Considerations of woman are also different.
She had already entered into compromise with the petitioner and does not want to prosecute him.

10. In view of compromise between the parties and considering the facts of the case, nature and manner in which offence is said to have been committed, the possibility of conviction is remote and bleak and continuation of criminal case will lead to unnecessarily waste of judicial time in trial where there is no hope of conviction and considering the judgment passed by Apex Court in case of Gian Singh (supra), present application under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. is allowed.
11. Accordingly, FIR as well as Sessions Trial No.214/2023 and consequential proceedings are quashed.
12. Copy of this order be sent to the trial Court for information.
